page: Microsoft Azure F8ams_v6 is a memory-intensive virtual machine belonging to the Famsv6 server family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 8 dedicated physical cores and 8 vCPUs powered by an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor operating at 3.7 GHz. The x86_64 architecture includes 32 KB L1d cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache per core, alongside advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 (including VNNI and BF16), AES, VAES, and SHA_NI. The system is equipped with 64.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high resource density of 8.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include local storage or integrated GPUs, but it is premium storage capable.

In benchmark testing, the F8ams_v6 demonstrates strong single-core performance, placing in the top 25% for stress-ng single-core CPU execution and Geekbench single-core scores. Text processing is a notable strength, ranking in the top 10% of Geekbench tests. Multi-core performance, including stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core metrics, falls within the average range. A key hardware tradeoff is observed in memory subsystem performance: while cached small-block read bandwidth and large-block write bandwidth are average, the uncached large-block read-only memory bandwidth is weak, placing in the bottom 25% at 38.03 GB/sec.

Given its high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 1:8 and dedicated CPU allocation, this server type offers qualitative cost efficiency for memory-bound workloads that do not require local NVMe storage. It is suitable for database operations, text processing pipelines, single-threaded decompression tasks, and small-scale language model inference, where text generation speeds for a 135M parameter model reach a strong 308.41 tokens/sec.
